main_issue: Who should wash the shellfish-contaminated shared pan now (so D can cook), and whether a wash-after-use rule fixes things going forward

A-B.evidence: Both deny using the pan and refuse to clean it (T1, T4, T15, T17); B accepts A's rule 'Fine' (T8) but asks about now, and A has no answer (T9).

A-C.evidence: C pushes that it's in 'our sink' and everyone lives here (T13); A insists 'it's not my mess to clean up' (T17).

A-D.evidence: D says someone must clean the pan (T14); A refuses to clean it (T15, T17), though A's rule (T7) addresses the future.

B-C.evidence: C: 'So you're just leaving it for the rest of us?' (T11); B: 'It's not my pan' (T12); C: 'We all live here' (T13).

B-D.evidence: D says none of that helps (T14) needing the pan cleaned; B says the pan isn't his and leaves to bed (T10, T12), though B says 'that doesn't make the pan clean' (T16).

C-D.evidence: C acknowledges 'Agent D needs to cook' (T5); D agrees 'Yes, I do' (T6) and D wants the pan cleaned (T14) while C argues it's a shared responsibility (T13).
